A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAM2Long and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and references. The complete documents, including v3 Appendices A–D, support comparison; substantial content can be matched across relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original SAM2Long segmentation and tracking results, parameter ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative comparisons in Tables 1–9 and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and adds diagnostic experiments, subgroup results, and qualitative cases, including Tables 9–12 and Figure 4 in the appendices.

M1.justification: The constrained tree search, cumulative log-IoU scoring, uncertainty-based mask selection, object-aware frame filtering, and memory-attention modulation remain unchanged. v3 explicitly describes separate trees per target, without establishing a procedural change. Temporal and spatial selection alternatives are additional ablations rather than adopted method components.

E1.justification: v3 Table 4 adds DAVIS-2017 evaluation. YouTube-VOS, both LVOS versions, the other segmentation benchmarks, and all three tracking benchmarks already have results in v2. Expanded dataset descriptions and revised headline benchmark counts therefore do not represent wholesale new coverage.

E2.justification: v3 removes RDE and SwinB-AOT from the SA-V comparison, CFBI and DeAOT from the LVOS comparison, and SAMURAI and DAM2SAM from the tracking comparison. This substantially narrows comparator coverage, including two directly relevant SAM-based trackers. The retained tracking baseline loses its SAM2.1 label but keeps identical scores; this does not establish a new comparator.

E3.justification: Additional diagnostic protocols include broader threshold grids, temporal/spatial selection controls, rounding-on/off comparisons with pairwise mask IoU, and separate evaluation of 73 single-object and 82 multi-object SA-V sequences. Efficiency reporting adds absolute FPS and memory consumption. The central first-frame-prompted benchmark evaluation remains stable.

E4.justification: The existing SA-V parameter ablations are expanded to LVOS and broader sensitivity sweeps. New analyses test temporal/spatial memory selection and whether IoU rounding produces diverse masks. Appendix C adds single-/multi-object analysis, while Figures 3–4 add a failure case and revised qualitative examples. These substantially expand evidence about mechanisms, robustness, and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The method's uncertainty handling concerns mask selection, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds DAVIS results, LVOS ablations, selection/diversity measurements, subgroup scores, and qualitative findings. Existing values also change: SAM2Long-L on LVOS in Table 1 goes from 85.2 to 85.4; SAM2Long SA-V validation in Table 2 from 79.7 to 80.8; SAM2.1Long YTVOS from 88.7 to 88.8. The SA-V score at uncertainty threshold 5 changes from 80.5 to 78.8. These are revised reported results, without evidence establishing reruns or a method improvement.

T1.justification: The memory definitions, cumulative scoring equation, frame-admission condition, and modulation-weight equations remain equivalent. Neither version develops theorems or proofs. The new pairwise mask-IoU experiment adds empirical analysis rather than mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The central training-free improvement to long-video segmentation is retained. v3 broadens the abstract's headline to nine VOS and three VOT benchmarks and changes the average gain from 3.0 over 24 comparisons to 3.7 over 12. The latter matches the SAM2-only subset, although Table 1 still contains 24 pairs, including SAM2.1.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations linking rounding to mask diversity and expanded sweeps to cross-dataset robustness. Its new failure case is attributed to reliance on fine visual details and insufficient semantic understanding. The conclusion explicitly identifies frozen SAM2 capacity as a limitation. The existing multi-object limitation is retained but now qualified using subgroup evidence.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents shared reproduction settings and common hyperparameter defaults, whose values already appeared in v2 ablations. It adds RTX 3090 hardware information for throughput and memory measurements, clarifies separate target memories, supplies further dataset/version descriptions, and adds a project-page link. These are documentation additions rather than demonstrated changes to existing experimental settings.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work newly ground the memory tree in Multiple Hypothesis Tracking, citing Reid, Cox and Hingorani, and Kim et al. v3 also contrasts mask-level memory selection with STCN/XMem feature-level approaches. The standalone SAM-applications discussion and associated citations disappear, as do SAMURAI/DAM2SAM references. This revises the central research positioning beyond citation formatting.

P1.justification: Dataset descriptions move into Appendix A and threshold analyses into Appendix B; tracking results move before ablations. The standalone SAM-related-work subsection is removed, and additional appendix sections, explicit limitations, and acknowledgments appear. Introduction, results, and qualitative discussion are substantially revised, while most method prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column document. Figure 1 replaces the balloon example with dancers while retaining the performance curves. The qualitative collection is rebuilt across Figures 3–4 with success/failure markers. Ablation tables are restructured for cross-dataset results, and efficiency columns add FPS and memory usage; the core Figure 2 pipeline is retained.

improvement.justification: The new mask-diversity test, broader sensitivity studies, and explicit failure example better justify the unchanged method and clarify its limits. MHT attribution and hardware/default disclosures also improve the paper. The net gain is limited by removed SAMURAI/DAM2SAM comparisons and reporting inconsistencies: v3 Table 2 gives an aggregate of 80.8 alongside J = 74.7 and F = 84.7. These shortcomings prevent a substantial overall improvement.
